name: a bent rusty metal sheet, broken concrete lumps, glass shards and a torn cable lying on an oil-stained patch of earth
label: wasteland_ruins/rubble-c

surfaces.part: bent rusty metal sheet with debris, three small clusters

answer.evidence: The main body is a full-width earth patch (64 px wide on every row, rows 0-47). It is a speckled brown ground texture with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical south face. The column scans show only mottled earth tones (L about 100-120), with small debris spots such as metal and glass highlights at x=47 rows 7-9 and 38-42. The sheet, concrete and cable clusters are small flat details lying on the ground and have no front faces of 3 or more rows. The whole object reads as a flat top-down decal, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The earth patch is a speckled, grainy brown soil with several distinguishable brown steps, comparable to the grass reference's grain and not a flat fill. Measured facts support this: 6 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, 1% near-flat coverage, and only 3% near-neutral dark edge pixels. That means the edges are tinted rather than a black sticker outline. The debris pieces (metal sheet, concrete lumps) are small clusters with light highlights and dark-brown edges, and they sit in the soil rather than floating on it. Weaknesses: the debris is sparse and small, and the oil stain, glass and cable are barely readable at this scale. The structure and shading craft still hold up next to the references, so I pass it, though not by a wide margin.
